one_month_reasoning: The only scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings after the close on Tue 2026-10-20 (src 31: consensus EPS ~$2.64, revenue ~$2.91B; ISRG has beaten EPS four quarters running). The key number is US da Vinci procedure growth, which slowed to 12% in Q2 from 14% in Q1 (src 19, 21, 22); management guided full-year 13.5-15.5% 'near the midpoint', which implies H2 deceleration, and the Q2 beat still produced a -12% reaction (src 22), so the bar is US procedures and the first color on 2027, not EPS. Against that, the stock has already run ~+15% from $350 (Sep 8) to $406-415 in late September (src 29) on EU SP approvals (src 36) with no change in fundamentals, which removes some of the easy upside on a merely in-line print, while short interest is low (2.31% of float, src 26) so there is little squeeze fuel. Other in-window items are slow: the Ninth Circuit en banc petition in SIS (filed 9/28, src 16) will not be decided in weeks; J&J Q3 (mid-Oct) may give the first Ottava placement color (src 20), a mild negative headline risk. Net: no directional edge; near-symmetric distribution centred at ~$401-404 with ~10.5% upside / ~12% downside one-month log sigma (37%/3.5 plus an earnings-gap bump, slightly fatter left tail given the pre-print run-up and the July reaction pattern).

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Expected-value litigation haircut applied after the blend (not weighted): SIS remand plus certified hospital class action (trial 2027-09-14)

inputs_detail.derivation: SIS itself is small ($140M claimed, $420M trebled, src 17). The real exposure is the hospital class (US EndoWrist/service purchasers May 2017-Dec 2021, trial 9/14/27, src 2), which the 9th Cir. SIS ruling strengthens (src 5) unless the en banc petition filed 9/28/26 succeeds (src 16). The court vacated its earlier aftermarket-monopoly finding in July 2024 (src 2). Assume ~25% chance of an adverse result worth ~$5-6B trebled pre-settlement plus modest pressure on usage-limit economics; already partly blunted because Intuitive honors 510(k)-cleared remanufactured instruments (src 24). Cut from -$6 in round 1 given the SIS damages size.

bear.story: US procedure growth keeps sliding (12% in Q2 toward ~9-10%) as ACA-subsidy losses are followed by 2027 Medicaid work-requirement disenrollment (~2.3M), first 2027 guide lands ~11-12%; Ottava and Hugo win price-sensitive accounts; China tenders keep going to domestic robots; hospital class trial (Sep 2027) heads toward an adverse verdict; USMCA review or a Section 232 device proclamation hits Mexicali/German supply. ~$12.0 EPS x 24x.

base.story: Low-to-mid-teens procedure growth, dV5 trade-in cycle and OUS (+20%) offset US softness, GM holds ~68%, EPS slightly below consensus, multiple drifts down 1-2 turns; litigation unresolved or settled for low $B. ~$13.4 2028 EPS x 32x.

bull.story: US softness proves transitory (BTIG view), dV5 and new indications keep procedures ~15%, tariff refunds and USMCA exemption hold, Ottava/Hugo stay sub-scale, en banc rehearing granted or class settles cheaply; re-rate to ~40x on ~$13.7.

thesis_break_reason: A close near/below $300 (~25% below today, under the $328.57 52-week low and ~25x 2027 consensus EPS) would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than volatility: a 2027 procedure guide near ~10%, evidence of US share loss to Ottava/Hugo or price cuts on dV5, an adverse hospital-class verdict/injunction undermining EndoWrist usage-limit economics, or loss of the USMCA tariff exemption for Mexico-made instruments. Unchanged from round 1: the new evidence moved inputs slightly in both directions but not the level at which the story itself would be wrong.

reasoning: Continuation of round 1 with ~20 more searches/reads, mostly in the skeptic lane. What changed: (1) Litigation is real but smaller than I framed: SIS claimed only $140M ($420M trebled); the meaningful exposure is the hospital class (purchases 2017-2021, trial 9/14/27), the 9th Cir. reversal helps those plaintiffs, but Intuitive filed for en banc rehearing on 9/28 and the district court had already vacated its aftermarket-monopoly finding; haircut trimmed to -$5. (2) Tariff fear overstated: the Q2 10-Q shows Mexicali instruments remain USMCA-exempt from the Section 122 10% tariff, IEEPA refunds are being received, GM guide was raised to 68-69%, and the Section 232 device probe has no proclamation; this lifts my 2028 EPS to $13.40. (3) Bariatric is only ~2% of procedures, so GLP-1 is a minor drag. (4) On the other side, the bear evidence firmed: US procedure growth 12% in Q2 vs 14% in Q1, ACA-subsidy effects confirmed by management and Citi, Medicaid work requirements from 1/1/27 (~2.3M disenrolled), Ottava already cleared on 7/22/26 (not pending as I had it), Hugo in US urology, China tenders ~half domestic. (5) No short-seller report, short interest only 2.31%, insider sales are tiny 10b5-1 trades; no credit angle (no debt). (6) Price: the stock ran ~+15% from $350 on Sep 8 to $414 on Sep 28 on EU approvals, so the setup into Q3 is less washed-out than it looked. Net fair value $421 (from $415); scenarios 25% $290 / 50% $425 / 25% $550 (mean ~$423). Ladder: split lognormal with ~31% up / ~37% down log-sigma (around the 37% realized vol, fatter left tail for litigation/competition/coverage), P(>=401) ~0.52.
